To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Hall coefficient near two dimensions vanishes at the critical point as (T-T(c))^g, with g=1.

the critical behavior of a system with particle-hole symmetry breaking is governed by a new scaling operator, that the Hall conductivity is nonanalytical near the metal-insuitor transition and that the critical behavior is not captured by perturbative methods.

the Hall conductivity is nonanalytic in the disorder strength at the mobility edge and that its behavior is governed by a scaling function that depends on a new scaling variable that is not related to the perturbation in the magnetic field.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the critical behavior of a quantum phase transition, which is induced by the introduction of disorder.
the scaling theory of the Hall conductivity near the metal-insu- itor transition.
the critical behavior of disordered systems near a disorder-driven phase transition.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the critical properties of Hall conductivity in the two-dimensional case are governed by the scaling variable g = 1, which is the same as the one governing the critical behavior of conductivity in two dimensions.
the Hall number is not a universal quantity and it vanishes with a nonuniversal exponent at the mobility edge.
the Hall conductivity, in the presence of disorder and a weak magnetic field, exhibits critical behavior with an exponent g=1 in two dimensions and g=1/2 in three dimensions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a field-theoretic renormalization-group theory to investigate the scaling behavior of Hall conductivity in the vicinity of the metal-insulator phase transition and the theory predicts that the critical exponent for the vanishing of Hall conductivity at the mobility edge is g = 1.
the field theory approach is the only way to study the Hall conductivity near the metal-insulation transition.

we have derived the renormalization group equations of the Hall conductivity close to the critical point and have shown that the perturbation in the field fails to capture the correct critical behavior of the weak field Hall conductivity.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the Hall number in the vicinity of the metal-insulator critical point can be obtained by a renormalization group analysis of the effective lagrangian describing the interactions of the time-reversal symmetric diffusive modes in weak magnetic fields.
the Hall number in two dimensions vanishes with an exponent g=1 at the mobility edge and that the perturbatively calculated exponent, g=2 is not relevant in the weak-field regime.
the critical behavior of Hall conductivity is governed by the scaling variable that measures the ratio between the time-reversal breaking and the particle-hole breaking operators.
